adrs.title: The operator's gestures reach the private database through a private gateway container, one role per gesture
adrs.statusWritten: accepted (2026-11-08), ratified by the author in chat ("ratifie", "ratify"), the session having recommended it
adrs.deciders: Thibault Souris (author). Written by an agent session.
adrs.method: decision-loop: reality-check (provider 2.88.0 schema, the hoster's documentation and the phase 1 state), sourced state of the art, challenge, durable position

reopening.text: Reopen when Serverless Jobs can join a Private Network (Jobs FAQ or provider changelog), when a gesture needs more than 900 s, or when a second operator needs a separate credential.
reopening.watchedVia: the provider upgrade review, the gateway's `operator.gesture` log lines (duration), the deploy's run summary

adrs.settles:
- **Confirms**: the first `roles`, `migrate` and `isolation` calls through the gateway answer 200 with `DATABASE_SSL=verify-full` against 172.16.16.2; a call without `X-Auth-Token` is refused by the hoster (HTTP 401 or 403, measured on the public endpoint, the gateway's log showing nothing); the two triggers have run at 03:23 and 03:37 Paris time on a day before and a day after a clock change.
- **Reverses**: a trigger that cannot reach a private container's path (then the schedule moves to a CI cron calling the gateway with the token), or the hoster forwarding a trigger without being able to authenticate it (then the token goes in a header from a sensitive variable and this ADR is superseded).
references: Scaleway: Serverless Jobs FAQ (Private Networks), Secure a container (private, `X-Auth-Token`, IAM conditions on the namespace), Use Serverless Containers with Private Networks, Add a trigger to a container (cron with time zone), all read 2026-11-08; provider `scaleway/scaleway` 2.88.0 schema (`scaleway_container`, `scaleway_container_trigger`).
ADR-0006 (one role per process, forced RLS), ADR-0008 (deploy by digest), ADR-0010 (operating with one human), ADR-0013 (no public database endpoint); `runward/runbook.md` §8, §11, §12.

adrs.title: Erasure empties every index version built from the erased content (refines ADR-0009)
adrs.statusWritten: accepted 2026-11-10 by the author in chat ("je suis ok pour tout ce que tu m'as cité", in answer to a list that named this record), after the independent review of `8fae95e` and its fixes
adrs.deciders: Thibault Souris (author). Written by an agent session.
adrs.method: decision-loop: reality-check (the store, the archive and the restore replay at `9e5728e`), a planted control on the old code, durable position; revised on 2026-11-10, while still proposed, after the independent review of `8fae95e` (`runward/governance/reviews/2026-11-10_code-review_8fae95e.md`, findings C21 to C26)

reopening.text: Reopen on 2026-12-10, or earlier when a column that projects content is added to `rw.fleet_index`, or when the index format changes (`runward-fleet-index/0`).

adrs.settles:
- **Confirms**: `test/unit/erasure.test.js` (11 cases) and `test/pg/erasure.test.js` (9 cases, as `rw_app` and as `rw_maint`) green, with the retention case of `test/pg/restore-replay.test.js`. They search a content marker in each version, object, journal entry and archive, as a superuser across tenants on PostgreSQL, with a positive control before the erasure and another tenant unchanged. A store that never empties a version reddens them. Four cases force, on two real connections, a transaction in flight during an erasure (an upload of another repository, an upload of the erased one, a change of language, a restore at the end of its window); two restore a backup of before a retention erasure.
- **Reverses**: an erased marker found in a version, an object or an archive; a legitimate change of a published version that the trigger refuses; a daily pass that fails on a tenant because of what it reads.
references: ADR-0009 (refined); PADR-0017

adrs.statusWritten: proposed (written by an agent session; acceptance is the author's)
adrs.deciders: Thibault Souris (author). Written by an agent session.
adrs.method: decision-loop: reality-check (the two commits of runward, the two tarballs, the same inputs built by each pin, an export archive of each pin replayed by the other), challenge, durable position

reopening.watchedVia: `scripts/verify-runward-fleet.mjs` in CI; the witness reader's daily summary and exit (`scripts/witness-reader.mjs`: a count of `not rebuilt here` above zero is visible in the summary, and a refused label or another archive after the pinned one makes the run red; the per-fleet JSON keeps each index's state); the service's start, which `fleetPin` refuses on another install; the release page of runward

adrs.settles:
- **Confirms**: `node scripts/verify-runward-fleet.mjs` green in CI against main@d05b597 (the 22 files are the pack of the commit, byte for byte, and nothing else is in the tarball); `test/unit/pin.test.js` green: the review's tarball (a second root, a missing file) refused in both modes, its table of labels (each one judged or the fleet not passed), an install that is not the archive refused, the three exits of the replay, the witness reader's rule and words; the router's own `resolve` answering null for `decision`; `/api/version` serving the sha256 of the tarball npm installed.
- **Reverses**: a file of the tarball that differs from main@d05b597 on GitHub, a file packed there and missing from the tarball, or an entry npm would install that is not one of them (the online check refuses each, and exits 2 rather than 0 when it cannot read the commit; before the review of 3afe41d, finding C40, it compared only the files under `package/` and a second root or a missing file passed); a view the app shows that breaks on an index of the previous archive; or the author deciding that a re-pin must republish every tenant's index, which needs its own record (a journaled gesture, and what the export then says of the versions before).
references: ADR-0018 (refined), ADR-0002, ADR-0004, ADR-0019; PADR-0011 points 4 and 6, note 6 bis
